references.notes: The photographs show the stair side, the central two-headed arch with carved flanking reliefs, the open side passages, and the low molded perimeter walls with incised and raised figures. The view from the enclosure shows the clay shoulders curving across the side returns and under the arches. In the close portal photo the left pier has a wide face over a low animal, and the right pier has two upright figures. Two dark stones stand in front. One has oversized circular eyes and folded arms. The other has two vertically stacked carved faces.

references.notes: Printed page 9 gives the Ataoja stool coordinate. The site plan on printed page 12 and the First Palace description on printed page 28 locate the courtyard in relation to the processional path and adjacent river bend.

limitations: The model represents the gateway, adjoining sculpted walls and the two small stone figures beside the central opening. The First Palace, Arugbá Gate, freestanding Èṣù sculpture and footbridge are separate structures.
The stairs, real-world dimensions, figures and rear-wall details are reconstructed from photographs.

The public tour provides the camera coordinate. The fit estimates the gate footprint, signed facing and scale from the panoramas. The immediate slope and enclosure beyond the three bays remain approximate.

panorama.coordinateBasis: The public virtual tour returns the camera latitude and longitude together with the panorama ID in its map metadata.
panorama.measured: The open bays, carved face panels and receding wall bases are visible. On the central stair landing, a dark band of small irregular pebbles curls back around a gap and trails toward the stair flight.
